answer: Each agent commits an epoch-locked state root: a Blake3 hash over a dedicated 32 GB array seeded with the sonnet epoch nonce, making the zenith layout unique per identity. The agent writes the array, seals cache-line proofs with nanosecond stamps, then publishes it. Verifiers re-derive a random slice under a fresh seed inside a 900 ms deadline; any mismatch slashes the 500 POA bond and freezes the identity. One honest agent holds 32 GB for one root; 10 fakes must hold 320 GB across 10 distinct machines, scaling cost linearly, with the timber trail public.
